question: According to the Agri-Food Fraud Network report (2023)1, systematic illegal movement of animals is being observed through the abuse of ‘non-commercial movement’ (Regulations 576/2013, 577/2013). The use of falsified documents, the circumvention of health controls and the loss of traceability pose serious risks to public health and biosecurity in the Union, as well as to animal welfare.

At the same time, complaint CPLT(2025)02624 of the Federation of Animal Welfare Associations of Greece documents the failure of the Greek authorities (judicial, police, veterinary, etc.) to enforce Regulation 2016/429 and the case law of the CJEU (C-301/14).

Incidents of commercial trade in pet animals from non-approved establishments (Regulation 2019/2035), the non-use of the TRACES system (Regulation 2020/688) and the use of falsified passports have been recorded. The infringements found are accompanied by the failure to impose effective and proportionate deterrents, in breach of Article 139 of Regulation 2017/625 and Article 268 of Regulation 2016/429.
In view of the above: 1.
Having regard to complaint CPLT(2025)02624, how does the Commission assess Greece's compliance with EU law?
What stage has the examination of this complaint reached and what further steps does the Commission intend to take?
What specific measures does the Commission intend to take to ensure the full implementation of control obligations and the imposition of truly effective and proportionate deterrent sanctions?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (13.4.2026) Τhe Commission can confirm that it received a complaint against Greece on the alleged illegal movement of pets and failure to implement EU law. It is examining the complaint in line with the Commission Communication on ‘EU Law: Better Results through Better Application’1.

The complainant will be informed of the findings of the examination and of any steps taken concerning the complaint once the examination has been completed. The Commission continues to ensure an appropriate follow-up within the remit of its competence of all information relating to possible non-compliance with the rules on the movement of dogs, cats or ferrets from Greece.
1 Communication from the Commission – EU law: Better results through better application, C/2016/8600, OJ C
